reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the handoff's refund claims against the refunds table itself. Starting with list_refunds.
The refunds table matches all three requested refunds in amount and order ID, so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list from the orders table.

All three refunds match the refunds table in both order ID and amount, so I can proceed. The orders table has three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 31766 cents. Checking against the orders table: acme has orders 140 (17469) and 143 (27956), totaling 45425, and order 140 has a 13659 refund, so 45425 - 13659 = 31766. That matches. Next I'll check birch.
Birch's balance of 35795 checks out: orders 141 (21876) and 144 (33383) total 55259, and the 19464 refund on order 144 leaves 35795. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's balance of 11416 checks out: orders 142 (8761) and 145 (12156) total 20917, and the 9501 refund on order 145 leaves 11416. All three refunds match the table and all three balances match my arithmetic, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 31766.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 35795, which I already checked against the orders and refunds tables.
Cobalt's payout is the only one left. Its balance of 11416 matches the orders and refunds I checked, so I'll record it now.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched the orders and refunds tables, so the batch is complete.
